findings.title: Automatic refresh can overwrite a fresh session after logout
findings.trigger: Session A keeps valid access while its refresh credential expires; the new expiry callback starts getRefreshToken, then the user logs out and logs in as Session B before the response returns.
findings.impact: The response interceptor passes the late refresh response to handleRefreshToken, which unconditionally stores Session A's refresh credential. A later relogin sends that revoked credential and the error path clears Session B's fresh access.
findings.fix: Bind the refresh response to the initiating session or generation, reject it after logout or login, and add an automatic-expiry after-login race assertion.
findings.verification: Run a retained test with an access-valid refresh expiry, delayed old response, logout, new login, and relogin. Assert the new session keeps its refresh credential and access token.
unverified_conditions: The retained race uses a direct refresh acquisition; a new automatic-expiry harness should be retained for exact end-to-end trigger binding.
Logout revocation and provider response timing are represented by local synthetic adapters.
